stories.headline: 5.3 magnitude earthquake strikes Nepal, tremors felt across five countries
stories.title: 5.3 magnitude earthquake strikes Nepal, tremors felt across five countries
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 24: A magnitude 5.4 earthquake struck near Lelep in Nepal’s Koshi Province at around 7:02 am on Tuesday, sending tremors across parts of India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and China. According to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS), the earthquake originated at a depth of 20 kilometres, with its epicentre at 27.855° N latitude and 87.909° E longitude. In India, tremors were felt in Jalpaiguri district of West Bengal, triggering panic among residents, who rushed out of their homes. No casualties or damage to property have been reported so far.

stories.headline: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
stories.title: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
stories.summary: The talks focused on establishing engagement protocols, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, and maintaining open communication channels
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India and China have concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh and putting in place measures to prevent friction between troops deployed along the frontier ahead of the onset of harsh winter conditions.
Sources in the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the closely guarded discussions, which began on November 8, 2026, a day after Deepavali, continued for nearly 10 days, with a short break in between.
The talks were described as cordial, though it remains unclear whether the measures discussed will be implemented on the ground before winter sets in fully.
Lieutenant-General Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Army’s III Corps, also known as the Spear Corps, led the Indian delegation.
The formation is headquartered at Rangapahar near Dimapur in Nagaland.
His Chinese counterpart and other military officers participated in the discussions.
An official from the Ministry of External Affairs was also present.

The latest round of talks primarily focused on establishing engagement protocols between the two sides, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, maintaining open communication channels and reducing tensions in the eastern sector.
Both countries have deployed substantial numbers of troops in the region.

The discussions assume significance as winter conditions along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh can become extremely severe, posing considerable challenges to troop sustenance, movement and logistical support.
Any delay in implementing the measures discussed could complicate the situation on the ground as temperatures fall and access to forward areas becomes increasingly difficult.
The second round follows the first Corps Commander-level meeting, held on September 6 and 7, 2026, at the Wacha-Damai Border Personnel Meeting (BPM) point in the Kibithoo sector.

stories.headline: Ousted leader Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on Dec 16, spokesperson says
stories.title: Ousted leader Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on Dec 16, spokesperson says
stories.summary: Dhaka, Nov 24: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, the day the country celebrates as Victory Day when it won independence after a war with Pakistan. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule. She was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity involving the uprising in which hundreds of protesters were killed. Hasina rejected the verdict and has said she is ready fight the case once she is back. In the statement Tuesday announcing the planned date of her return, she urged current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline. “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali said in the statement. “It is deeply symbolic that she has chosen 16 December, our Victory Day, for her planned return to Bangladesh. We firmly believe that she will celebrate this historic day among her people, honouring the great victory achieved under the leadership of her father, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman," Abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Hasina, told The Associated Press. “We are equally confident that, she will definitely return and under her leadership post return, Bangladesh will once again advance towards peace, stability and prosperity,” Arin said. Earlier this month, in an interview with The Associated Press, Hasina said she would return to the country in December at any cost, and even death could not prevent her from returning home.

stories.headline: Global brands eye India for textile sourcing
stories.title: Global brands eye India for textile sourcing
stories.summary: New Delhi: Global brands are increasingly exploring India as a textile and apparel sourcing destination as changes in US tariff structures, new free trade agreements (FTAs) and supply-chain disruptions in competing countries create fresh opportunities for Indian exporters, according to a report by Dolat Capital.The report said changes in US tariffs and FTAs have improved India's competitiveness, bringing it at par with Bangladesh and other Asian peers while retaining an advantage over China and Vietnam.This could support India's efforts to attract more international orders as global buyers look to diversify their sourcing destinations.It said, "India's relatively competitive sourcing position and the implementation of the India-UK FTA providing a potential boost to order flows".India's trade agreements are also expected to strengthen its position in key export markets. The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), implemented on July 15, 2026, provides duty-free access to Indian garments and home textiles, potentially supporting orders from the UK.The proposed India-EU FTA, expected in early 2027, could remove India's approximately 12 per cent duty disadvantage against least-developed countries (LDCs), further improving the competitiveness of Indian textile exporters.The report expects the benefits of these trade agreements to become more visible from FY28 as global buyers realign their sourcing strategies. The report also noted that order books for several Indian apparel manufacturers are looking encouraging for Q3FY27.Supply-chain challenges in competing manufacturing destinations are creating additional opportunities for India. Labour disruptions and proposed wage revisions in Bangladesh, along with higher manufacturing costs due to inflation in Turkey, are encouraging global brands to diversify sourcing towards India, Egypt and Morocco.It stated, "Meanwhile, labour disruptions and wage revisions in Bangladesh and a proposed minimum wage increase in Bangladesh... along with high inflation in Turkey, are encouraging global brands to diversify sourcing towards India and other manufacturing destinations".The report said multi-country sourcing strategies are gaining traction as international brands increasingly prioritise supply-chain resilience.India is also benefiting from changing demand patterns in China. Higher domestic cotton prices in China, at around USD 1.00 per pound, and restrictions on Xinjiang cotton have made local yarn production less competitive.This has supported Indian yarn exports to China, which are estimated at around 20-25 million kg per month as Chinese manufacturers increasingly source from India.The report said capacity expansion, higher vertical integration and a shift towards value-added products are expected to support growth, although elevated raw material costs and the pace of margin recovery remain key factors to watch.

opening: New Delhi: Global brands are increasingly exploring India as a textile and apparel sourcing destination as changes in US tariff structures, new free trade agreements (FTAs) and supply-chain disruptions in competing countries create fresh opportunities for Indian exporters, according to a report by Dolat Capital.
The report said changes in US tariffs and FTAs have improved India's competitiveness, bringing it at par with Bangladesh and other Asian peers while retaining an advantage over China and Vietnam.
body: This could support India's efforts to attract more international orders as global buyers look to diversify their sourcing destinations.
It said, "India's relatively competitive sourcing position and the implementation of the India-UK FTA providing a potential boost to order flows".

The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), implemented on July 15, 2026, provides duty-free access to Indian garments and home textiles, potentially supporting orders from the UK.

The proposed India-EU FTA, expected in early 2027, could remove India's approximately 12 per cent duty disadvantage against least-developed countries (LDCs), further improving the competitiveness of Indian textile exporters.
The report expects the benefits of these trade agreements to become more visible from FY28 as global buyers realign their sourcing strategies.
The report also noted that order books for several Indian apparel manufacturers are looking encouraging for Q3FY27.
Supply-chain challenges in competing manufacturing destinations are creating additional opportunities for India.

Labour disruptions and proposed wage revisions in Bangladesh, along with higher manufacturing costs due to inflation in Turkey, are encouraging global brands to diversify sourcing towards India, Egypt and Morocco.
It stated, "Meanwhile, labour disruptions and wage revisions in Bangladesh and a proposed minimum wage increase in Bangladesh...
along with high inflation in Turkey, are encouraging global brands to diversify sourcing towards India and other manufacturing destinations".
The report said multi-country sourcing strategies are gaining traction as international brands increasingly prioritise supply-chain resilience.
India is also benefiting from changing demand patterns in China.
Higher domestic cotton prices in China, at around USD 1.00 per pound, and restrictions on Xinjiang cotton have made local yarn production less competitive.
This has supported Indian yarn exports to China, which are estimated at around 20-25 million kg per month as Chinese manufacturers increasingly source from India.

The report said capacity expansion, higher vertical integration and a shift towards value-added products are expected to support growth, although elevated raw material costs and the pace of margin recovery remain key factors to watch.

Police Officers' Association (KPOA) and redistributing its members between two other associations.

A bench of Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva put on hold the Division Bench ruling of November 12, 2026, which had set aside a Single Judge decision quashing the government's restructuring order dated July 27, 2026.

Police Association (KPA), the Kerala.
Police Officers' Association (KPOA) and the Kerala.
Police Senior Officers' Association (KPSOA).
Under the restructuring, the State had decided to abolish the KPOA and redistribute its members between the KPA and KPSOA.

Police Officers, Senior Civil Police.

Officers, Grade Assistant Sub Inspectors, Assistant Sub Inspectors and Grade Sub Inspectors under the KPA, while directly recruited Sub Inspectors and officers in the regular promotional hierarchy, including Inspectors, Deputy Superintendents of Police and Superintendents of Police (Non-IPS), would be grouped under the KPSOA.

The associations challenged the government order before the Kerala High Court, arguing that the existing associations functioned under government-approved bylaws and their organisational structure could not be altered contrary to those rules.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu Government Moves Supreme Court Challenging Madras HC Order To Remove Periyar Statue From Temple Land
stories.title: Tamil Nadu Government Moves Supreme Court Challenging Madras HC Order To Remove Periyar Statue From Temple Land
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Tamil Nadu Government has approached the Supreme Court challenging the Madras High Court's order directing the removal of a statue of Dravidian movement leader and reformer EV Ramasamy, popularly known as Periyar, installed near the Arulmigu Bramasirakandeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur district.

The Madras High Court, by its order dated October 30, 2026, had directed the Thanjavur District Collector to safely remove the statue from the temple land and relocate it to another suitable place within four weeks.
The Court had also directed the State authorities to file a compliance report and listed the matter after four weeks to verify compliance.

The Division Bench comprising Justices P Velmurugan and K Ramakrishnan passed the order while hearing a writ petition filed by Rama Ravikumar, a devotee, seeking the removal of the statue from the temple premises.

The petitioner had sought the removal of the statue in light of a recommendation made by the Joint Commissioner of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department, Thanjavur, in proceedings dated July 8, 2026.
The petitioner had alleged that the statue was installed by the Dravidar Kazhagam in 1990 without obtaining the necessary permission from the HR&CE Department.
He had also objected to the inscription beneath the statue, which carries Periyar's statement denying the existence of God.

During the proceedings, the High Court had directed the District Collector to conduct a physical inspection of the location and ascertain whether the statue stood on temple land or government poramboke land.
The authorities subsequently informed the Court that the statue was situated on land belonging to the temple and not on government poramboke land.

Taking note of the status report submitted by the District Collector, the Bench observed that the statue had been installed on temple land without obtaining permission from the temple authorities, the District Collector or any other competent authority.
Accordingly, the Court directed the District Collector to remove the statue safely and relocate it to another suitable place within four weeks.
The Court disposed of the writ petition with the above directions and ordered the matter to be listed after four weeks for reporting compliance.

stories.headline: Political leaders, environmentalists seek ecological protection
stories.title: Political leaders, environmentalists seek ecological protection
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 23: Political leaders, environmentalists, and civil society groups on Monday called for an investigation into the use of heavy machinery near Sheshnag Lake, raising concerns over possible damage to the ecologically fragile glacial landscape. A video circulating on social media showing a crawler excavator digging and levelling ground near Sheshnag, a high-altitude glacial lake in south Kashmir's Pahalgam area, has triggered widespread concern and demands for an immediate halt to the activity. The footage shows the machine cutting into the ground, moving earth and dumping soil along the Amarnath Yatra route near the lake. Initially shared by an excavator operator before being deleted, the video has raised questions about the precise location and nature of the excavation, the agencies involved and its possible environmental impact. CPI(M) MLA from Kulgam Muhammad Yusuf Tarigami, who also chairs the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly's Committee on Environment, called for an immediate halt to the activity and an inspection by glaciologists and environmental experts. Expressing concern over videos purportedly showing heavy machinery being used for road development along the Amarnath Yatra track, Tarigami said Sheshnag was among the 14 high-risk glacial lakes identified in Jammu and Kashmir. He said the lake was surrounded by loose moraine and steep slopes, making the terrain particularly vulnerable to disturbance. "Disturbing this fragile terrain with heavy machinery is an invitation to disaster," Tarigami said in a statement. He said nobody was opposed to development and that pilgrims, tourists and local residents deserved better roads and facilities. However, infrastructure development in the high Himalayas must be guided by scientific studies, environmental impact assessments and consultations with experts and local communities. Referring to the 2013 Kedarnath disaster, the 2023 South Lhonak Lake disaster in Sikkim and a recent glacier-related disaster in Nepal, Tarigami cautioned against human interference in fragile mountain ecosystems. He warned that the potential consequences could extend downstream to Pahalgam, settlements along the Lidder and other parts of south Kashmir. Tarigami sought details of the project, the executing agency and the clearances obtained, besides an immediate halt to any work that could threaten the lake and its surroundings. "Development cannot and should not come at the cost of such a disaster," he said. Former chief minister and PDP President, Mehbooba Mufti, said the issue was very painful, and criticised the government for watching as mere spectators. "The government itself is having Chinar trees cut down. At the university, they are cutting down our old walnut trees. They just watch as spectators and don't say a word. Our Kashmir will become another Uttarakhand. What can we say? When they built roads and expressways for the Char Dham Yatra, look at how many storms and calamities strike there today. It is very bad," she said. "The issue is very painful." However, she said that if her party says anything more on the issue, it will be accused of being against the Amarnath Yatra. "If we talk about it, they will say we are against the Amarnath Yatra. What can I say? They try to polarise everything," she told reporters here. National Conference (NC) Lok Sabha MP Mian Altaf said it is essential to safeguard Kashmir's lakes. "I have not seen that, so I cannot say anything to you about it. I will just say that Kashmir's lakes must be saved. They must be saved at any cost. Its rivers must be saved, its forests must be saved. That is essential for all of us, essential for Kashmir, for Kashmir's tourism, for Kashmir's environment, and for our health," Altaf said. Apni Party President and former minister Altaf Bukhari said authorities must clarify whether the video showing a JCB operating near Sheshnag Lake was authentic. "If the video is genuine, the government owes the public a clear explanation: What is such heavy machinery doing in an ecologically fragile zone, especially around a high-altitude glacial lake?" he said. Bukhari said Kashmir had already suffered the consequences of unchecked construction and human interference, resulting in the loss of glaciers, water bodies and natural habitats. He said authorities must act responsibly, ensure transparency and protect the region's natural heritage, adding that development should not come at the cost of environmental destruction. Former Lok Sabha MP from Srinagar, Syed Aga Ruhullah, said Kashmir's mountains are not the BJP's real estate. "A party that wins votes in the name of faith is now taking JCBs to a holy lake. First, the BJP pushed motor roads up to the Amarnath cave. Now heavy machinery is digging at Sheshnag, a high-risk glacial lake. "Nepal just showed us what happens when the Himalaya is treated like a construction site. Stop this now. Kashmir's mountains are not BJP's real estate," Ruhullah said in a post on his official handle on X. Kashmir's chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq also termed the visuals disturbing, saying glacier retreat and recent glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal should serve as a warning about the vulnerability of the Himalayan region. "Kashmir has always warmly welcomed Amarnath Yatra pilgrims, and improving facilities for them has never been an issue. But not at the cost of our fragile ecosystem," Mirwaiz wrote on X. He demanded an immediate halt to the activity, saying the region's mountains, glaciers and water bodies needed protection for present and future generations.
